abstract: Clinical stage I seminomas are effectively treated with surgery raising concerns as to when to give adjuvant radiation therapy given the risk of secondary malignancies. A recent randomized trial found tumor size and rete testis invasion to be the strongest predictors of relapse in clinical stage I seminomas. These 2 parameters may be surrogate measures of tumor volume. Intertubular seminoma (ITS) of the testis describes the presence of neoplastic germ cells within the interstitium of the testis. These cells are detected away from the main macroscopic mass. Because ITS can infiltrate in a 3-dimensional fashion, it may also represent a measure of tumor volume not usually noted in standard pathology reporting. The goal of this study was to determine the incidence of ITS in pure seminomas and its association with other prognostic parameters. One hundred twenty consecutive pure seminomas surgically removed between 1998 and 2003 were evaluated. ITS was defined as the presence of an interstitial or intertubular growth pattern of tumor cells, which was noncontiguous with the main tumor and present at least 3 high-power fields away from the tumor mass. The average tumor size was 3.4 cm. Of the entire cohort of patients, which included pathological stages T1 through T3, 11% had invasion through the tunica albuginea, 51% had rete testis invasion, 51% had lymphovascular invasion, 93% had associated intratubular germ-cell neoplasia, and 36% had ITS. ITS was significantly associated with rete testis invasion ( P = .001). Logistic regression analysis looking at ITS, tumor size, patient age, and lymphovascular invasion revealed that only ITS was associated with rete testis invasion (RR, 4.1, P < .0001). ITS is present in a significant proportion of pure seminomas and has a significant association with rete testis invasion. The presence of ITS may therefore be an important prognostic factor, not only because it alters the calculated size of the tumor but also because it has an association with rete testis invasion.
abstract_ja:
背景：臨床病期Iのセミノーマは外科的切除で効果的に治療されるが、続発性悪性腫瘍のリスクがあるため、補助放射線療法をいつ行うかが問題となっている。最近のランダム化試験では、臨床病期Iのセミノーマにおける再発の最も強い予測因子は腫瘍径と精巣網浸潤であった。この2つのパラメータは腫瘍体積の代用指標となる可能性がある。精細管間セミノーマ(ITS)は、精巣間質内に存在する腫瘍性の胚細胞を指す。これらの細胞は主腫瘍から離れた部位で検出される。ITSは三次元的に浸潤しうるため、標準的な病理報告では通常記載されない腫瘍体積の指標となる可能性もある。
目的：純粋セミノーマにおけるITSの頻度と、他の予後因子との関連を明らかにすること。
方法：1998年から2003年の間に外科的切除された連続する純粋セミノーマ120例を評価した。ITSは、主腫瘍から非連続的で、少なくとも3高倍率視野以上離れた、間質性または精細管間の増殖パターンを示す腫瘍細胞と定義した。
結果：平均腫瘍径は3.4cmであった。病理学的病期T1からT3を含む全症例のうち、11%が白膜浸潤、51%が精巣網浸潤、51%がリンパ管侵襲、93%が精細管内胚細胞腫瘍を伴い、36%がITSを有していた。ITSは精巣網浸潤と有意に関連していた（P = .001）。ITS、腫瘍径、患者年齢、リンパ管侵襲を検討したロジスティック回帰分析では、精巣網浸潤と関連したのはITSのみであった（RR 4.1, P < .0001）。
結論：ITSは純粋セミノーマの相当な割合に認められ、精巣網浸潤と有意な関連を持つ。ITSは腫瘍サイズの算定を変えるだけでなく、精巣網浸潤との関連から、重要な予後因子となりうる。
